Title: Random Forests
Authors: Breiman L.
Research_Problem: Ensemble learning via bagged decision trees
Main_Findings: Random Forest outperforms single trees; built-in feature importance via Gini impurity
Limitations: No XAI beyond Gini importance; no imbalance handling
Relation_to_Our_Work: Foundation for our RF classifier

Title: SMOTE: Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique
Authors: Chawla NV; Bowyer KW; Hall LO; Kegelmeyer WP
Venue: Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research vol.16 pp.321-357
Research_Problem: Class imbalance in binary classification
Main_Findings: SMOTE interpolation generates effective minority samples; improves minority-class recall
Limitations: Does not address multiclass NIDS; no XAI; no feature attribution analysis
Relation_to_Our_Work: Foundation for our SMOTE rebalancing step

Title: Scikit-learn: Machine Learning in Python
Authors: Pedregosa F et al.
Research_Problem: Python machine learning library
Main_Findings: Unified API for ML in Python; integrated with NumPy/SciPy
Limitations: N/A
Relation_to_Our_Work: Library used for RF; preprocessing; evaluation in our experiments

Title: UNSW-NB15: A Comprehensive Data Set for Network Intrusion Detection Systems
Authors: Moustafa N; Slay J
Research_Problem: NIDS benchmark dataset creation
Main_Findings: Dataset with 9 modern attack types from controlled testbed; 175k training / 82k test split
Limitations: Single environment; potential concept drift
Relation_to_Our_Work: Primary dataset in our study

Title: "Why Should I Trust You?": Explaining the Predictions of Any Classifier
Authors: Ribeiro MT; Singh S; Guestrin C
Research_Problem: Post-hoc local interpretable explanations
Main_Findings: LIME produces locally faithful linear approximations; model-agnostic; applicable to any classifier
Limitations: Stochastic sampling causes instability across runs; computationally expensive
Relation_to_Our_Work: LIME used for secondary XAI in our study

Title: Imbalanced-learn: A Python Toolbox to Tackle the Curse of Imbalanced Datasets in Machine Learning
Authors: Lemaître G; Nogueira F; Aridas CK
Research_Problem: Python library for imbalanced learning
Main_Findings: Comprehensive toolbox extending scikit-learn for imbalanced data
Limitations: Library; not a study
Relation_to_Our_Work: Library used for SMOTE in our pipeline

Title: A Unified Approach to Interpreting Model Predictions
Authors: Lundberg SM; Lee SI
Research_Problem: Unified framework for feature attribution using Shapley values
Main_Findings: SHAP unifies LIME; RISE; DeepLIFT under game-theoretic framework; TreeSHAP is exact and efficient
Limitations: Global SHAP requires marginalisation over training data; correlated features can distort values
Relation_to_Our_Work: Primary XAI method (SHAP TreeExplainer) in our study

Title: From Local Explanations to Global Understanding with Explainable AI for Trees
Authors: Lundberg SM; Erion G; Chen H et al.
Research_Problem: Scalable exact SHAP for tree ensembles; local-to-global explanations
Main_Findings: TreeExplainer computes exact SHAP in polynomial time; enables global understanding from local explanations
Limitations: Specific to tree models; SHAP values depend on feature correlation structure
Relation_to_Our_Work: Direct algorithmic basis for our SHAP TreeExplainer application

Title: Explainability of SMOTE Based Oversampling for Imbalanced Dataset Problems
Authors: Patil A; Framewala A; Kazi F
Research_Problem: Interpretability of SMOTE-generated data
Main_Findings: SMOTE oversampling with interpretable models shows decision boundaries can shift; feature importance changes post-balancing
Limitations: No SHAP; no Wilcoxon/statistical tests; no NIDS context; single dataset
Relation_to_Our_Work: Closest prior work to our study: examines SMOTE + explainability but not in NIDS; no effect-size analysis

Title: Intrusion Detection Model for Imbalanced Dataset Using SMOTE and Random Forest Algorithm
Authors: Alshamy R; Ghurab M; Othman S; Alshami F
Research_Problem: Multi-class IDS with SMOTE+RF on imbalanced NSL-KDD
Models: Random Forest; Logistic Regression; SVM; AdaBoost
Main_Findings: IDS-SMOTE-RF achieves high accuracy on NSL-KDD; outperforms LR/SVM/AdaBoost
Limitations: No XAI; no UNSW-NB15; no explanation stability analysis
Relation_to_Our_Work: SMOTE+RF IDS without XAI — demonstrates gap our study addresses

Title: Statistical Stability Indices for LIME: Obtaining Reliable Explanations for Machine Learning Models
Authors: Visani G; Bagli E; Chesani F; Poluzzi A; Capuzzo D
Venue: Journal of the Operational Research Society vol.73(1) pp.91-101
Research_Problem: LIME instability across repeated runs
Eval_Metrics: CSI (Coefficients Stability Index); VSI (Variables Stability Index)
Main_Findings: LIME produces different explanations across runs; CSI and VSI quantify this instability; LIME is inherently stochastic
Limitations: Validated only on credit risk data; not cybersecurity; no comparison with SHAP
Relation_to_Our_Work: Provides the stability-measurement framework we implicitly follow (Spearman correlation; top-k overlap)

Title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Cybersecurity: A Literature Survey
Authors: Charmet F; Tanuwidjaja HC; Ayoubi S; Gimenez PF; Han Y; Jmila H; Blanc G; Takahashi T; Zhang Z
Research_Problem: Survey of XAI methods applied to cybersecurity tasks
Main_Findings: XAI methods are increasingly applied to NIDS; SHAP and LIME are dominant; explanation evaluation remains an open challenge
Limitations: Survey — does not empirically compare explanation stability under distribution shift
Relation_to_Our_Work: Contextualises our work within the XAI-cybersecurity landscape; highlights gaps we address

Title: Intrusion Detection System Combined Enhanced Random Forest with SMOTE Algorithm
Authors: Wu T; Fan H; Zhu H; You C; Zhou H; Huang X
Venue: EURASIP Journal on Advances in Signal Processing vol.2022 art.39
Research_Problem: NIDS class imbalance with SMOTE+RF hybrid
Main_Findings: K-means SMOTE + enhanced RF improves minority-class detection; large train/test accuracy gap suggests overfitting
Limitations: Train/test gap; no XAI; no UNSW-NB15
Relation_to_Our_Work: SMOTE+RF IDS — we extend this by adding SHAP/LIME analysis and UNSW-NB15

Title: Effect of Data Resampling on Feature Importance in Imbalanced Blockchain Data: Comparison Studies of Resampling Techniques
Authors: Alarab I; Prakoonwit S
Venue: Data Science and Management vol.5(2) pp.66-76
Research_Problem: How SMOTE and other resampling change feature importance rankings in imbalanced data
Main_Findings: Resampling changes feature importance rankings; SMOTE produces largest feature rank shifts in this domain
Limitations: Blockchain context only; no NIDS; no SHAP/LIME; no statistical tests; no effect-size analysis
Relation_to_Our_Work: Most closely related to our work in terms of resampling + feature importance; but no NIDS; no SHAP/LIME; no Wilcoxon tests

Title: A Survey on Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Cybersecurity
Authors: Rjoub G; Bentahar J; Abdel Wahab O; Mizouni R; Song A; Cohen R et al.
Venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management vol.20(4) pp.5115-5140
Research_Problem: Systematic survey of XAI for cybersecurity
Main_Findings: XAI methods improve transparency in cybersecurity; SHAP and LIME dominate NIDS XAI; explanation evaluation is under-studied
Limitations: Survey — no empirical evaluation; no class imbalance focus
Relation_to_Our_Work: Strongest motivation source: identifies explanation evaluation under distribution shift as an open problem

Title: Enhanced Intrusion Detection Systems Performance with UNSW-NB15 Data Analysis
Authors: More S; Idrissi M; Mahmoud H; Asyhari AT
Research_Problem: Comparative ML evaluation on UNSW-NB15
Models: Logistic Regression; SVM; Decision Tree; Random Forest
Main_Findings: Random Forest achieves best F1=97.80%; accuracy=98.63% on UNSW-NB15; feature correlation analysis used
Limitations: No XAI; no class imbalance treatment; no minority-class analysis
Relation_to_Our_Work: Establishes RF as the dominant baseline on UNSW-NB15 — consistent with our model choice

Title: Explainable AI for Intrusion Detection Systems: LIME and SHAP Applicability on Multi-Layer Perceptron
Authors: Gaspar D; Silva P; Silva C
Research_Problem: Applying LIME and SHAP to explain MLP-based IDS for IoT
Dataset: IoT traffic (specific dataset unverified — access full text to confirm)
Main_Findings: LIME provides intuitive local explanations; SHAP provides consistent global rankings; both improve IDS transparency
Limitations: No class imbalance treatment; MLP only (no tree models); no explanation stability under distribution shift
Relation_to_Our_Work: Most direct prior comparison: LIME+SHAP on IDS — but no SMOTE; no RF; no stability comparison across models

Title: Enhanced Intrusion Detection with LSTM-Based Model Feature Selection and SMOTE for Imbalanced Data
Authors: Sayegh HR; Dong W; Al-madani AM
Research_Problem: IoT-NIDS with SMOTE for class imbalance using LSTM
Main_Findings: SMOTE + LSTM improves rare attack-class detection in IoT NIDS; feature selection reduces dimensionality
Limitations: No XAI; no UNSW-NB15; no explanation analysis
Relation_to_Our_Work: SMOTE-based NIDS without XAI — reinforces the gap: rebalancing is common but its XAI effect is not studied

Title: Addressing Class Imbalance in Intrusion Detection: A Comprehensive Evaluation of Machine Learning Approaches
Authors: Shanmugam V; Razavi-Far R; Hallaji E
Research_Problem: Comprehensive ML evaluation under varying class imbalance levels in NIDS
Models: RF; SVM; KNN; Naive Bayes; others
Main_Findings: Resampling strategies vary in effectiveness depending on degree of imbalance; RF with SMOTE performs consistently
Limitations: No XAI; no UNSW-NB15; no feature attribution analysis
Relation_to_Our_Work: Confirms SMOTE+RF as competitive baseline for imbalanced NIDS — our work adds the missing XAI layer

Title: Explainable AI for Forensic Analysis: A Comparative Study of SHAP and LIME in Intrusion Detection Models
Authors: Hermosilla P; Berríos S; Allende-Cid H
Research_Problem: Comparative SHAP and LIME analysis on IDS using UNSW-NB15
Eval_Metrics: Accuracy (97.8% XGBoost); fidelity; consistency; forensic relevance
Main_Findings: XGBoost outperforms TabNet in explanation stability; SHAP and LIME are complementary; combined deployment recommended
Limitations: No class imbalance treatment; no SMOTE; no statistical tests on explanations; no RF
Relation_to_Our_Work: Closest to our work in SHAP+LIME on UNSW-NB15 — but no balancing; no RF; no Wilcoxon/effect-size analysis

Title: Use of Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Analyzing and Explaining Intrusion Detection Systems
Authors: Hermosilla P; Díaz M; Berríos S; Allende-Cid H
Research_Problem: XAI framework evaluation for IDS explanation analysis
Main_Findings: XAI methods improve understanding of IDS decisions; SHAP is more globally coherent; LIME more locally variable
Limitations: No class imbalance handling; no statistical comparison; no SMOTE
Relation_to_Our_Work: Companion work to P20 — both complement our contribution by not addressing rebalancing effects
